digest.headline: The sudden surge of brand‑new AI‑agent skill repos like ayghri/i-have-adhd and Tencent/teamai-cli eclipses long‑standing favorites, while veteran archify disappears entirely
digest.digest:
This week’s most eye‑catching story is the record‑breaking star velocity of ayghri/i-have-adhd, which hit an all‑time high of 4,624 stars per day on its third day. The repo introduces a "coding‑agent ADHD" skill that forces LLM‑driven agents to surface answers instead of burying them in lengthy context, a niche need that resonated strongly with developers building autonomous code assistants. Its rapid rise is amplified by a fresh release that adds configurable interruption thresholds, turning a quirky concept into a practical productivity hack.

A second surprise comes from Tencent/teamai-cli, a brand‑new CLI for synchronizing AI‑agent skills that amassed 1,083 stars per day on debut. The tool fills a gap left by fragmented skill‑management workflows, offering a single command‑line interface to version, test, and deploy agent capabilities across multiple environments. Its immediate popularity suggests that teams are now treating agent skill sets as first‑class code artifacts, a shift not evident from the category chart alone.

While newcomers dominate, several long‑running heavy‑hit repos vanished from the list, most notably tt‑a1i/archify, which had held the top‑star velocity spot for weeks with architecture‑diagram generation. Its disappearance hints at a possible release fatigue or a shift in community focus toward more agent‑centric tooling. In contrast, sustained performers like bilawalsidhu/gods-eye-view (photorealistic 3D globe visualizer) and obra/superpowers (agent‑enhanced development environment) continue their multi‑day runs, underscoring that visual and developer‑experience tools still retain a loyal audience despite the AI‑skill frenzy.

The week also marks a structural pivot in category composition: Productivity repos surged to 27 entries, overtaking Developer Tools (25) and AI/ML (23). This is driven by a cluster of new productivity‑oriented projects such as melgarafael/DeskcommCRM, a three‑day‑trending CRM built for remote teams, and jihe520/MathModelAgent, which automates mathematical modeling workflows. Their emergence reflects a broader move to embed AI assistance directly into everyday work tools rather than isolated AI research demos, a nuance that the raw category percentages alone would miss.
